about: Step 3B PR 4b answer key (tests/delivery/expected/passages.json), written by the controller by hand before the code, by reading the committed synthetic new-format handoffs under the rulings P1 to P10 (3B controller, 2026-11-15) and D1 to D4, D14, D22, C14. `documents`: every builder on each committed fixture as it stands. `marked`: one builder on a fixture after the listed text replacements (each `old` occurs exactly once in the fixture; apply them in order). `refused`: the builder named refuses (the typed delivery refusal); one row per refusal kind (R24 condition 1). `cells`: [cell text, expected cell, expected [unit, currency] of the figure behind `at`, or null when `at` is null], where `at` is a decimal string or null (R24 condition 2: the caller never draws positions of different unit, scale word or currency against each other). `leaks`: [text, source names, expected matches in text order]. `names` for a document is its own Sources-table names (handoff.data.source_names). Every name and figure is invented. Implementers do not edit this file.

bottomLine.label: Bottom line
bottomLine.lead: The canonical data set holds the debt, cash, earnings and maturity figures the later modules rely on, each tied to a page of the two documents read.

bottomLine.label: Bottom line
bottomLine.lead: Northbridge is a single-segment services group whose creditors depend on one operating company, so debt service rests on that company's cash generation.

findings.lead: The group earns almost all its cash in one operating company, which concentrates creditor risk there.
Two debt dates fall within 24 months and drive the refinancing question.
Results are published on a fixed quarterly rhythm, so new evidence arrives on a known schedule.

contrary.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
contrary.text: The strongest point against concern is the steady quarterly reporting record. A refinancing announced before the first debt date would soften the view.

limitations.text: The covenant package was not reviewed, so covenant headroom is not assessed.
Dates after the annual report are scheduled, not confirmed, so the nearest-date list may move.

bottomLine.label: Bottom line
bottomLine.lead: Creditors are exposed to refinancing risk rather than to weak earnings: net debt of USD 1,390 million is 4.2x earnings, and the next maturities fall inside two years.

findings.lead: Leverage is moderate but not low, at 4.2x net debt to EBITDA, so there is little room for an earnings miss.
A large part of the debt comes due soon: 38% of gross debt matures within 24 months, which makes refinancing access the deciding factor.
Liquidity support rests on an undrawn revolver that steps down, which narrows the cushion over time.

contrary.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
contrary.text: The strongest evidence against concern is the consistent earnings record over recent quarters. A signed refinancing of the nearest maturity would move the view towards comfort. The company has not said how it intends to fund the step-down.

limitations.text: The Covenant package was not reviewed,  so covenant headroom is not assessed
Peer leverage was not compared, so the 4.2x reading has no market anchor.
The liquidity assessment is not available, so cash cover of the maturities is unverified.
